translations.literal: (From the 《History of Song, Biography of Fu Yanqing》: At the time the Jin army was on the leeward side; as battle was about to begin, bows and crossbows could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《History of Song, Biography of Fu Yanqing》: The Jin army was then on the leeward side, and with battle imminent their bows and crossbows were useless.

sentences.zh: 彥卿謂張彥澤、皇甫遇曰：「與其束手就擒，曷若死戰，然未必死。

translations.literal: Yanqing said to Zhang Yanzhe and Huangfu Yu, "Rather than wait to be captured with hands bound, how much better to fight to the death—yet death is not certain.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing told Zhang Yanzhe and Huangfu Yu, "Better to fight to the death than be taken with hands bound—and we may not die at all.

sentences.zh: 」彥澤然之，遂潛兵尾其後，順風擊之，契丹大敗。

translations.literal: " Yanzhe agreed; he then sent troops secretly to follow behind them and struck with the wind—the Khitan were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhe agreed, sent troops quietly in their rear, struck with the wind at their backs, and the Khitan were routed.

sentences.zh: 又，《藥元福傳》：守貞與元福謀曰：「軍中饑渴已甚，若候風反出戰，吾屬為虜矣。

translations.literal: Further, from the 《Biography of Yao Yuanfu》: Shouzhen and Yuanfu plotted, saying, "The army is already desperately hungry and thirsty; if we wait for the wind to turn before fighting, we shall all become captives.
translations.idiomatic: Also from the 《Biography of Yao Yuanfu》: Shouzhen and Yuanfu plotted together, saying, "The troops are already desperate with hunger and thirst. If we wait for the wind to shift before fighting, we shall all be taken captive.

sentences.zh: 彼謂我不能逆風以戰，宜出其不意以擊之，此兵家之奇也。

translations.literal: They think we cannot fight against the wind; we should strike them unawares—this is a strategist's surprise move.
translations.idiomatic: They assume we cannot fight into the wind. We should strike where they do not expect it—that is the classic stratagem of surprise.

sentences.zh: 」元福乃率麾下開拒馬出戰，諸將繼至，契丹大敗。）〉

translations.literal: " Yuanfu then led his men, opening the chevaux-de-frise to give battle; the other generals followed, and the Khitan were utterly defeated.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu led his men out through the chevaux-de-frise; the other generals joined him, and the Khitan were routed.)〉

sentences.zh: 時步騎齊進，追襲二十餘里。

translations.literal: At the time infantry and cavalry advanced together and pursued for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry and cavalry advanced together and pursued the enemy for more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 至陽城東，賊軍稍稍成列，我騎復擊之，乃渡河而去。

translations.literal: East of Yangcheng the enemy army gradually formed ranks; our cavalry struck them again, and they then crossed the river and departed.
translations.idiomatic: East of Yangcheng the enemy slowly re-formed their ranks; our cavalry struck again, and they crossed the river and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「今日危急極矣，幸諸君奮命，吾事獲濟。

translations.literal: Shouzhen said, "Today was the utmost extremity of peril; thanks to you all fighting with your lives, our cause has been saved.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "Today brought us to the brink of ruin. Thanks to your desperate fighting, we have been saved.

sentences.zh: 兩日以來，人馬渴乏，今吃水之後，腳重難行，速宜收軍定州，保全而還，上策也。

translations.literal: For two days men and horses have been parched and exhausted; now that they have drunk water, their legs are heavy and hard to move—we should quickly withdraw the army to Dingzhou, preserve our forces, and return; that is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: For two days men and horses have gone without water. Now that they have drunk, their legs are heavy and marching is hard. We should withdraw quickly to Dingzhou, preserve the army, and return—that is the best course.

sentences.zh: 」由是諸將整眾而還。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the generals re-formed their troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The generals then re-formed their troops and marched back.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹主坐車中，及敗走，車行十餘里，追兵既急，獲一橐駝，乘之而走。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan ruler was seated in his carriage; when he fled in defeat, the carriage had gone more than ten li and the pursuers were pressing hard, so he obtained a camel, mounted it, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler had been seated in his carriage. When he fled in defeat, his carriage had gone little more than ten li before the pursuers closed in; he seized a camel, mounted it, and rode away.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，杜威等大軍自定州班師入恒州。

translations.literal: On yichou, Du Wei and the great army withdrew from Dingzhou in formal return and entered Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Du Wei and the main army marched back from Dingzhou and entered Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙子，以車駕將還京，差官往西京告天地宗廟社稷。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingzi day, because the imperial carriage was about to return to the capital, officials were dispatched to the Western Capital to report to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on bingzi day, with the emperor about to return to the capital, envoys were sent to the Western Capital to announce the return to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，駕發澶州。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the imperial carriage departed from Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the imperial procession left Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，至京師，曲赦在京禁囚。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor arrived at the capital and proclaimed a partial amnesty for prisoners held in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the emperor reached the capital and granted a partial amnesty to prisoners confined there.

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔鄴都依舊為天雄軍。

translations.literal: On jihai, an edict restored Yedu as the Tianxiong Army command.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, an edict restored Yedu to its former status as the Tianxiong Army command.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，河東節度使劉知遠封北平王；

translations.literal: On gengyin, Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, was enfeoffed as King of Beiping;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Liu Zhiyuan, military governor of Hedong, was enfeoffed as King of Beiping;

sentences.zh: 恒州節度使杜威加守太傅；

translations.literal: Du Wei, military governor of Hengzhou, was promoted to acting Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Du Wei of Hengzhou was promoted to acting Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 徐州趙在禮移鎮兗州；

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou was transferred to military governor of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili of Xuzhou was transferred to Yanzhou as military governor;

sentences.zh: 宋州節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步都指揮使高行周移鎮鄆州，侍衛如故；

translations.literal: Gao Xingzhou, military governor of Songzhou and overall commander of the Palace Guard horse and foot armies, was transferred to military governor of Yanzhou, retaining his guard duties;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou of Songzhou, overall commander of the Palace Guard armies, was transferred to Yanzhou as military governor while keeping his guard post;

sentences.zh: 鄴都留守馬全節改天雄軍節度使；

translations.literal: Ma Quanjie, garrison commander of Yedu, was made military governor of the Tianxiong Army;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Quanjie, garrison commander of Yedu, became military governor of the Tianxiong Army;

sentences.zh: 兗州節度使兼侍衛都虞候李守貞移鎮宋州，加檢校太師兼侍衛親軍副指揮使；

translations.literal: Li Shouzhen, military governor of Yanzhou and chief adjutant of the Palace Guard, was transferred to military governor of Songzhou, promoted to acting Grand Preceptor with concurrent post as deputy commander of the Palace Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen of Yanzhou, chief adjutant of the Palace Guard, was transferred to Songzhou as military governor, promoted to acting Grand Preceptor, and made deputy commander of the Palace Guard;

sentences.zh: 河中節度使安審琦加兼侍中，移鎮許州；

translations.literal: An Shenqi, military governor of Hezhong, was given additional concurrent title of Vice Director of the Secretariat and transferred to military governor of Xu Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: An Shenqi of Hezhong was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and transferred to Xu Prefecture as military governor;

sentences.zh: 許州節度使符彥卿加同平章事，移鎮徐州；

translations.literal: Fu Yanqing, military governor of Xu Prefecture, was promoted to Grand Councillor and transferred to military governor of Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing of Xu Prefecture was made Grand Councillor and transferred to Xuzhou as military governor;

sentences.zh: 滑州節度使皇甫遇加同平章事。

translations.literal: Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was promoted to Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Yu, military governor of Huazhou, was made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，西京留守景延廣加邑封，改功臣；

translations.literal: On renchen, Jing Yanguang, garrison commander of the Western Capital, received an increase in fief and a change in merit-title;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Jing Yanguang, garrison commander of the Western Capital, received an enlarged fief and a new merit-title;

sentences.zh: 泰州節度使侯益移鎮河中；

translations.literal: Hou Yi, military governor of Taizhou, was transferred to military governor of Hezhong;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi of Taizhou was transferred to Hezhong as military governor;

sentences.zh: 定州節度使王周加檢校太師。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou, military governor of Dingzhou, was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou, military governor of Dingzhou, was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.
